title: Telemetry shipping guidance and customer integration patterns
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact, implementation-focused guide for shipping Redwood telemetry to customer SIEMs (Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel). It consolidates pragmatic connector specs, minimal customer requirements, and integration patterns we can hand to Solutions/CS during onboarding. NOT a final spec — working draft with open questions and TODOs.

Context and goals:
- Customers want: structured audit logs + runtime events + operational evidence (traces/attachments) exported reliably to their SIEM.
- Constraints: data classification and PII redaction, throughput and rate limits, retention/forwarding windows, RBAC v2 context, and evidence-anchoring semantics.
- Goal: provide 3 supported export patterns (push via HEC/Logs API/HTTP Data Collector), a hosted relay option, and minimal mapping templates.

Terminology (short):
- Event = single JSON log line (audit or runtime).
- Evidence = attachments or snapshot artifacts (supporting compressed blobs or URLs) associated with an event.
- Connector = piece of software/config that forwards events from Redwood to customer SIEM.

Required fields for exported events (canonical audit schema) — minimal set (all fields must be present; empty values allowed only where noted):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC (e.g. 2026-02-14T15:04:05Z)
- event_type: audit | access | system | alert | evidence
- actor_id: internal user id or service principal (format: user:<id> | svc:<id>)
- actor_email: email when available (null allowed)
- action: string describing operation (e.g. "model.deploy", "request.generate", "rbac.grant")
- resource_type: e.g. model, project, route, key, capacity-pool
- resource_id: opaque id used by Redwood (prefer stable id)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- request_id: unique per HTTP request (traceable to tracing/span id)
- trace_id: distributed trace id when available (null allowed)
- client_ip: masked IPv4/IPv6 (see privacy rules)
- region: region code (e.g. us-west1)
- keystate: optional (kms-key-id or "customer-managed")
- rbv2_claims: compact string summary of RBAC v2 context (see below)
- message: human-friendly summary (short)

Mapping guidance for each SIEM
1) Splunk (HEC)
- Transport: HTTP Event Collector (HEC) with token auth. HEC index should be provided by customer during setup.
- Recommended HEC fields mapping: time -> timestamp, sourcetype -> "redwood:audit:v1" (customer may override), host -> redwood-inference, source -> "redwood/audit".
- Payload style: send raw JSON in "event" field; include top-level "fields" with metadata (region, cluster, team).
- Batch behavior: prefer batching up to 5MB or 5000 events, flush every 5s or when batch size reached.
- Splunk-specific caution: use gzip compression if >1MB and respect HEC rate limits; expose a per-customer backoff when 429.

2) Datadog Logs API
- Transport: HTTPS with API key. Use log intake endpoint with log-specific attributes: ddsource=redwood, service=inference, ddtags=customer:<id>.
- Mapping: timestamp, host, message, attributes -> JSON object of remaining fields.
- Rate limits: Datadog enforces daily ingestion quotas; surface quota errors to CS and fallback to S3-based buffer if configured.
- Recommended: set "status" property for alerts; mark evidence events with event_type=evidence and include evidence_url.

3) Microsoft Sentinel (Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector)
- Transport: HTTP Data Collector API with shared key or customer-managed agent.
- Mapping: Collector expects JSON array of records. Ensure event timestamp is included and use customLogName like Redwood_Audit.
- Chunking: Azure max payload ~30MB; recommended chunk <5MB for reliability.

Field redaction & PII rules (must be enforced before forwarding)
- Full redaction pipeline sits in Redwood; connectors must not perform ad-hoc redaction. Standard policy: remove sensitive fields (auth headers, full request bodies for user-supplied text unless customer opts in), mask IPs to /24 for IPv4 and /64 for IPv6, obfuscate email local-part (a***@domain.com), strip raw prompt contents unless explicit customer agreement.
- Evidence attachments: store in customer-specific S3 (or Redwood s3) and send secure short-lived URL in event (evidence_url) with access audit attached. If evidence contains PII, mark evidence.is_pii=true and require approval in onboarding.

Authentication & Secrets
- Splunk: HEC token (recommended rotate every 90 days).
- Datadog: API key scoped to logs only.
- Sentinel: workspace id + shared key or managed identity for private deployments.
- For Dedicated/Private customers: support mTLS to on-prem collectors.

Delivery guarantees & retry policy
- Primary mode: at-least-once delivery.
- Connector should implement exponential backoff with jitter: base=1s, max=120s, max_attempts=10 before marking event into durable dead-letter store.
- For rate-limit responses (HTTP 429): respect Retry-After header. Implement circuit-breaker per-customer for persistent failures (5 consecutive 429/5xx -> pause for 10 minutes and escalate).

Evidence automation (how to attach logs and snapshots to a support case)
- Evidence events should include: evidence_type, evidence_url, evidence_digest (sha256), evidence_size_bytes, evidence_ttl (seconds).
- Support flow: when customer raises an incident ticket, CS runbook can query events by request_id and attach evidence_url(s) to the ticket. We prefer push-notify to the customer's ticketing system via webhook; see onboarding checklist.

Connector configuration templates (examples to hand to customer)
- Splunk HEC snippet:
  url: https://input-prd-p-XXXXX.cloud.splunk.com:8088/services/collector/event
  token: HEC_TOKEN_REDACTED
  index: redwood_audit
  batch_max_bytes: 5242880
  batch_max_age_seconds: 5

- Datadog Logs API snippet:
  url: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input
  api_key: DATADOG_API_KEY_REDACTED
  ddsource: redwood
  ddtags: customer:acme-inc,env:prod

- Sentinel snippet:
  url: https://<workspace-id>.ods.opinsights.azure.com/api/logs?api-version=2016-04-01
  shared_key: SHARED_KEY_REDACTED
  customLogName: Redwood_Audit

Operational: monitoring & alerts for export reliability
- Metrics to surface in Console/Support: per-customer outgoing throughput (events/sec), average latency to SIEM (p50/p95), error rate (4xx, 5xx), last successful delivery timestamp, dead-letter queue size.
- Recommended alert thresholds (first pass):
  - Error rate > 2% sustained for 10m -> P1 investigation.
  - No successful delivery for 30m -> P1.
  - Dead-letter queue growth > 1k events in 1h -> P2.

Onboarding checklist for Solutions/CS (minimal customer requirements)
- Customer provides: target endpoint URL(s), token/key, preferred index/log name, ingestion rate expectations, retention SLA, IP allowlist (if used).
- Data classification sign-off: which fields are allowed; explicit consent for forwarding prompt contents and evidence attachments.
- Test plan: run 1 hour smoke tests (low-volume), verify indexing and field mappings, validate redaction and PII handling, confirm evidence_url access and TTL.
- Fallback plan: if ingestion fails, we must agree on alternate path (S3 bucket with notification or email) and retention policy for buffered data.

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we standardize on a single "rbv2_claims" compact format or send full RBAC object? Sending full object is heavy but more flexible. (Action: Ravi to prototype compact claim string 2026-02-21)
- Evidence size policy — current proposal: max 50MB per evidence blob. Need legal sign-off for larger artifacts.
- Data residency: for private deployments, customer may require all evidence to remain on-prem. Add sample on-prem agent config.
- Metric tagging: include customer_id tag on all metrics emitted by connector itself for billing/observability.

Appendix: small examples
- Example audit event (JSON):
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-02-14T15:04:05Z",
    "event_type": "audit",
    "actor_id": "user:U-12345",
    "actor_email": "a***@example.com",
    "action": "model.deploy",
    "resource_type": "model",
    "resource_id": "m-9876",
    "outcome": "success",
    "request_id": "req-5b9c",
    "trace_id": "trace-001",
    "client_ip": "10.0.0.0",
    "region": "us-west1",
    "rbv2_claims": "org:acme;role:admin;env:prod",
    "message": "deployed model m-9876 via console"
  }

- Evidence event example:
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-02-14T15:05:00Z",
    "event_type": "evidence",
    "evidence_type": "model-trace",
    "evidence_url": "https://s3.redwood.example.com/e/abc123?sig=...",
    "evidence_digest": "sha256:abcd...",
    "evidence_size_bytes": "2345678",
    "evidence_ttl": "3600",
    "request_id": "req-5b9c"
  }

Notes to CS/solutions engineers (quick):
- Always request ingestion test keys and do a low-volume smoke run. Confirm that customer SIEM parses JSON fields (some customers rely on regex extraction in Splunk; prefer JSON ingestion).
- If customer uses heavy regex-based parsing on their side, document field names we send and provide a sample event for their index team.

Contact & ownership: Elena Park (security-infra) — reach out on #sec-telemetry with questions.
